title: Saturated integral Tate-module embedding and finite generation of homomorphisms of abelian varieties
author_responsibility: J. S. Milne supplies the statement and complete argument in fixed 2022 AVs Theorem 12.5.
material_provenance: Complete author statement, integral-divisibility lemma and proof from the fixed corrected AVs PDF. Earlier AV I.10.15 and the erratum remain separately identified.
difficulty_reason: For a finite independent set of endomorphisms of a simple abelian variety, Milne uses the degree polynomial to get a real discrete lattice and a common denominator. The l-adic relation would contradict this denominator after divisibility descends from Tate modules to algebraic endomorphisms. He then passes to products of simple factors up to isogeny.

readability.basis: Original AVs 2022 corrected author PDF. The same PDF holds the complete theorem, divisibility lemma and proof.

source_caveats: For arbitrary abelian varieties over k and l distinct from char(k), preserve injectivity, torsion-free cokernel and the finite-free rank bound. No Galois equivariance or claim of Tate surjectivity.

The 2008 proof has the error identified by Timo Keller: the degree polynomial is applied on the wrong ambient module and finite-dimensionality is assumed when taking a Q-basis. The same-author corrected AVs proof instead starts with each finitely generated M, obtains its denominator and rules out an l-adic relation. The sources remain separately identified.

The finite-rank consequence of the injective map and the preceding lattice argument give the stated finite generation. AVs cites the standard discrete subgroup lattice theorem and its previously proved degree polynomial.

source_disclosures.author: J.S. Milne
source_disclosures.erratum_summary: The earlier proof applies the degree polynomial with M in the wrong ambient module and assumes finite dimensionality when choosing a rational basis for End^0(A). The selected corrected proof is the separately fixed 2022 AVs Theorem 12.5.
